title: What If It Rained in California for 43 Days Straight?

scenes.text: What if it rained on California for forty-three days straight? It already did once.
In the winter of 1861 to 62, nearly ten feet of rain fell in parts of the state, and the Central Valley became an inland sea about 300 miles long.
Sacramento sat under about ten feet of water. Roughly one in eight houses was destroyed or swept away, and 200,000 cattle drowned.
A modern version, the USGS ARkStorm scenario, imagines storms for more than 25 days, hundreds of landslides, and up to 1.5 million people evacuated.
Losses are estimated near 725 billion dollars, with power, water, and sewer outages lasting weeks to months.
Geologists find major California floods roughly every hundred to two hundred years. The last one this big was 1862.
